text:
mira: quick check — customer hit duplicated partial output when a short streaming call (client sends prompt, model returns ~1-2s) had an upstream transient and gateway retried. behavior: client saw two chunks, second started mid-sentence. wondering what we expect from gateway for short-lived streams: transparent retry, early abort, or require client resume token?
aj: can you paste the request + response headers (redact ids)?
mira: logs below, removed ids. headers: 
```
:method: POST\n:path: /v1/streams/generate
:authority: api.redwood.io
content-type: application/json
x-resume-token: (none)
x-client-id: app-42
```
response stream fragments: first TCP connection closed by upstream at chunk 3/5. gateway retried to fallback model without resume token; client received chunk 1..3 then 4..5 overlapping.
aj: ugh. two immediate axes: (1) require resume token on streaming calls (client-managed) so gateway can resume without re-sending tokens, OR (2) gateway attempts transparent restart but must ensure idempotent delimiter/trailer so clients can dedupe.
ryan: for short streams I prefer gateway-transparent if we can cheaply detect overlap window. but detection is brittle. if we add an opaque resume token header generated by gateway upstream we can make resume deterministic. downside: client changes.
sam: also consider side effects. some streams trigger webhooks or DB writes mid-stream (rare, but). transparent retry risks duplicate side effects. resume-token only helps for read-only generation.
mira: good point. this case was pure generation (no side effects) but we should generalize.
aj: proposal sketch: 
- require client to opt-in to gateway resume by sending `x-enable-resume: true` for short streams.
- gateway will return `x-resume-token` in trailers when closing normally.
- on upstream transient, gateway will attempt single transparent retry only if resume token present; otherwise surface error to client.
- for hedged fallbacks (parallel models) mark trailers with `x-duplicate-id` to help clients dedupe.

ryan: +1 but clarify hedging semantics: if we fan-out to fallback model and both return, who owns final trailers? gateway should canonicalize trailer selection and only forward the first-complete set. second response must be dropped server-side, maybe logged with `duplicate=trace`.
sam: still worried about customer burden. opt-in is fine, but we should strongly default for PLG users to disabled and enable for Dedicated customers.
mira: operational note: this requires adding trailer plumbing across our proxy pool and ensuring we can persist resume tokens across small window (few secs). cheap if token is stateless HMAC of last-k-bytes + model id.
aj: security: resume token must be scoped to client and model-version; otherwise a malicious client could replay against another tenant. include tenant id and short TTL.
ryan: one more tradeoff: for very short calls (<200ms) the overhead of token generation might add latency. we can make token generation async and only attach when call exceeds N bytes/time.
mira: action items:
- aj: write a short RFC for `x-enable-resume` + trailer contract (deadline Thu EOD).
- ryan: prototype token HMAC scheme and perf test (next week).
- sam: scope billing/side-effect doc update and default policy for tiers.
aj: noted. I'll add a sample proto for trailers in the RFC.
deploy-bot: deploy-check — staging passes for proxy-trailer-changes :white_check_mark:
mira: thanks — small decision for now: opt-in resume + single transparent retry only when token exists. we can iterate. :thumbsup:
aj: cool, moving to RFC channel when ready.
ryan: fyi, I'll drop a short log snippet showing overlap detection algorithm in the RFC.
sam: added to my calendar to review RFC on Thu.
mira: closing the thread — please ping if you disagree.
